Magnitude: The Local Open Source Definitive AI Engine (Rode LLMs on your PC!)

Magnitude is a local and open source inference engine to run AI models on the computer you already have. The video shows how it analyzes the hardware and chooses the model, loads the models on demand, protects the memory and connects to programming agents.

Published in 11 September 2026 · 8 min 22 s

  • AI tools

Open on YouTube

Why local AI is difficult

A lot of people want an AI 100% private and unsigned, but the technical effort to make it work is a barrier. 00:00. Magnitude is a local and open source inference engine that tries to remove this barrier 00:22.

Who has configured models at home knows the cycle of trial and error: GGUF files, quantization limits that can spoil the model and locking due to lack of memory 00:43.

Cloud AI is powerful, but has continuous cost, risk of privacy and limits of use 01:46. The traditional local AI is free and private but unstable and difficult to adjust 02:08. According to the video, the current hardware has plenty of power; an orchestrator was missing 02:08.

End of manual configuration

Magnitude does the work in four steps 02:28:

  • Analyze the available processor and memory 02:28.
  • Catalog and rank the best model combinations 02:50.
  • Download and configure everything by yourself 02:50.
  • Start the model already connected to the agent of your preference 02:50.

The ranking weighs the expected speed, model quality and quantization, and compares the size of the context window with the memory that really remains 03:12.

It runs on Apple Silicon, on NVIDIA and AMD cards and only on CPU, Linux and Windows by WSL 03:33.

Loading on demand

Before, climbing a model occupied much of the memory until the process was closed 04:15. In Magnitude, the models stay on the disk and only go to memory when an agent sends a command 04:15.

The video uses an analogy: the model is an encyclopedia on the shelf (the disk) that only goes to the table (the memory) at the time of reading and comes back later 04:35.

Memory management

Memory usage changes all the time because of the browser and other programs 05:16. Therefore, Magnitude confers real-time memory and only carries the model if there is safety margin 05:16.

  • Downloads templates when they are inactive 05:38.
  • Redo memory calculation before each new load 05:38.
  • Interrupt the inference if the memory falls too much, and preserves the prompt state not to lose context 05:38.

Integration with agents

Open templates usually have different reasoning formats and chat templates, which breaks tools 06:00. Magnitude normalizes this and presents a single interface, so the tools can switch models without rewriting code 06:22.

It works with Harness Magnitude and tools like Claude Code, Cline and Codex 06:43. The engine displays local APIs in OpenAI and Anthropic standards, so the agents talk to it as if talking to the cloud 07:03.

Cost and privacy

The cost of each call is zero: no tuition, no package of tokens and no API key 07:23. The code and the prompts don't leave the machine 07:23.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Magnitude run on Windows?

Yes, by WSL. Also runs on macOS with Apple Silicon and Linux 03:33.

The model keeps occupying the memory all the time?

Nope. The models stay on the disk and only go to memory when an agent asks, and are unloaded when they are inactive 04:15.

About the video

**Magnitue** is a local inference engine and *open source* designed to run the best AI models directly on the hardware you already own, whether it's a Mac, NVIDIA/AMD GPU or just CPU. Excuse me. Apache 2.0, it offers a 100% free, private solution without API costs or request limits.

In this video, we explain how Magnitude analyzes the processor, memory and bandwidth of your system to recommend the optimal combination of model, quantization and context size. In addition, we detail how your server in the background loads models on demand and connects natively to various agents and tools such as Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Oh My Pi and Cline.

---

**Quick Terminal Installation:**
'``bash
npm i -g @magnitudedev/cli
setup magnitude
```
*(You can also install using 'bun', 'pnpm' or 'yarn'). *

**Compatibility:**
Magnitude runs in **macOS**, **Linux** and **Windows (via WSL)**. The inference engine is developed in Rust on the llama. cpp and displays local APIs compatible with OpenAI and Anthropic on port `10100`.
